item.question: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and AC = 8 cm. Find OA, OC, OB and OD.
steps: In ∆AOB and ∆COD: AB = CD, ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite), and ∠ABD = ∠CDB (each is 90° minus the same angle).
By the AAS condition, ∆AOB ≅ ∆COD, so OA = OC and OB = OD.
The diagonals are equal, so BD = AC = 8 cm.
Each half is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.
item.answer: OA = OC = OB = OD = 4 cm; the strips are joined at their midpoints
item.text:
Worked example: In rectangle ABCD the diagonals meet at O and AC = 8 cm. Find OA, OC, OB and OD.
1. In ∆AOB and ∆COD: AB = CD, ∠AOB = ∠COD (vertically opposite), and ∠ABD = ∠CDB (each is 90° minus the same angle).
2. By the AAS condition, ∆AOB ≅ ∆COD, so OA = OC and OB = OD.
3. The diagonals are equal, so BD = AC = 8 cm.
4. Each half is 8 ÷ 2 = 4 cm.
Answer: OA = OC = OB = OD = 4 cm; the strips are joined at their midpoints

item.question: Equal diagonals bisect each other at 40°. Find the angles of the quadrilateral.
steps: In the triangle with 40° at O, the base angles add to 180 − 40 = 140, so each is 140 ÷ 2 = 70.
The next triangle has 180 − 40 = 140 at O, so its base angles add to 180 − 140 = 40, and each is 20.
Each corner of the quadrilateral is 70 + 20 = 90.
item.answer: All four angles are 90°, so it is again a rectangle
item.text:

3. Each corner of the quadrilateral is 70 + 20 = 90.
Answer: All four angles are 90°, so it is again a rectangle

item.question: The carpenter has one strip 8 cm long. How long must the other strip be for the thread to make a rectangle?
steps_tex: Model the strips as the diagonals $AC$ and $BD$ of a rectangle $ABCD$, with $AC = 8\text{ cm}$.
In $\triangle ADC$ and $\triangle DAB$: $AB = CD$, $\angle BAD = \angle CDA = 90^\circ$, and $AD$ is a common side.
By the $SAS$ condition, $\triangle ADC \cong \triangle DAB$.
So $AC = BD$, as corresponding parts of congruent triangles.
The other strip must be $8\text{ cm}$ long.

item.question: Two equal diagonals bisect each other and meet at 60°. Find all the angles of the quadrilateral ABCD and say what it is.
steps_tex: The four angles at $O$ are $60^\circ$, $120^\circ$, $60^\circ$ and $120^\circ$.
In $\triangle AOB$, $OA = OB$, so its two base angles are equal. Their sum is $180 - 60 = 120$, so each is $120 \div 2 = 60$.
In $\triangle AOD$ the angle at $O$ is $120^\circ$, so its base angles add to $180 - 120 = 60$, and each is $30$.
Each corner of $ABCD$ is made of one angle of each kind: $60 + 30 = 90$.
$\triangle AOB \cong \triangle COD$ and $\triangle AOD \cong \triangle COB$ by $SAS$, so $AB = CD$ and $AD = CB$.
item.answer_tex: Every angle of $ABCD$ is $90^\circ$ and its opposite sides are equal, so $ABCD$ is a rectangle
steps: The four angles at O are 60°, 120°, 60° and 120°.

In ∆AOD the angle at O is 120°, so its base angles add to 180 − 120 = 60, and each is 30.
Each corner of ABCD is made of one angle of each kind: 60 + 30 = 90.
∆AOB ≅ ∆COD and ∆AOD ≅ ∆COB by SAS, so AB = CD and AD = CB.
item.answer: Every angle of ABCD is 90° and its opposite sides are equal, so ABCD is a rectangle

steps_tex: Cross the two equal sticks so that their midpoints meet at $O$.
Pass the thread round the four ends of the sticks in order.
The sticks are equal diagonals that bisect each other, so the thread makes a rectangle.
Every corner of a rectangle is $90^\circ$, so the thread turns through an exact $90^\circ$ at each stick end.
item.answer_tex: Cross the sticks at their midpoints and run the thread round the four ends; each corner of the thread is exactly $90^\circ$

item.question: ABCD has all four angles 90°. Show that AD = CB and DC = BA, and say why writing ∆BAD ≅ ∆CDB is wrong.
steps_tex: Join the diagonal $BD$.
$\angle BAD = \angle DCB = 90^\circ$, and $BD$ is common to $\triangle BAD$ and $\triangle DCB$.
$\angle ABD + \angle DBC = 90^\circ$ and $\angle CDB + \angle DBC = 90^\circ$, so $\angle ABD = \angle CDB$.
By $AAS$, $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle DCB$, matching $B$ with $D$, $C$ with $A$ and $D$ with $B$.
So $AD = CB$ and $BA = DC$.
$\triangle CDB$ would match $D$ with $A$, but the right angle at $A$ has to match the right angle at $C$, not $D$.
item.answer_tex: $AD = CB$ and $DC = BA$; $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle CDB$ is wrong because the vertices are not in matching order
steps: Join the diagonal BD.
∠BAD = ∠DCB = 90°, and BD is common to ∆BAD and ∆DCB.
∠ABD + ∠DBC = 90° and ∠CDB + ∠DBC = 90°, so ∠ABD = ∠CDB.
By AAS, ∆BAD ≅ ∆DCB, matching B with D, A with C and D with B.
So AD = CB and BA = DC.
∆CDB would match A with D, but the right angle at A matches the right angle at C, not D.
item.answer: AD = CB and DC = BA; ∆BAD ≅ ∆CDB is wrong because the vertices are not in matching order
item.text:
$1$. Join the diagonal $BD$.
$2$. $\angle BAD = \angle DCB = 90^\circ$, and $BD$ is common to $\triangle BAD$ and $\triangle DCB$.
$3$. $\angle ABD + \angle DBC = 90^\circ$ and $\angle CDB + \angle DBC = 90^\circ$, so $\angle ABD = \angle CDB$.
$4$. By $AAS$, $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle DCB$, matching $B$ with $D$, $C$ with $A$ and $D$ with $B$.
$5$. So $AD = CB$ and $BA = DC$.
$6$. $\triangle CDB$ would match $D$ with $A$, but the right angle at $A$ has to match the right angle at $C$, not $D$.
Answer: $AD = CB$ and $DC = BA$; $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle CDB$ is wrong because the vertices are not in matching order

item.question: In rectangle ABCD, show that AB is parallel to DC.
steps_tex: Take $AD$ as a transversal to the lines $AB$ and $DC$.
The internal angles on the same side of $AD$ are $\angle A$ and $\angle D$.
$\angle A + \angle D = 90 + 90 = 180$.
Internal angles on the same side of a transversal adding to $180^\circ$ means the lines are parallel.
steps: Take AD as a transversal to the lines AB and DC.
The internal angles on the same side of AD are ∠A and ∠D.
Internal angles on the same side of a transversal adding to 180° means the lines are parallel.
item.text:

$2$. The internal angles on the same side of $AD$ are $\angle A$ and $\angle D$.
$3$. $\angle A + \angle D = 90 + 90 = 180$.
$4$. Internal angles on the same side of a transversal adding to $180^\circ$ means the lines are parallel.
Answer: $AB \parallel DC$

item.question: Find all the other angles inside the following rectangles. (i) Rectangle ABCD with diagonals meeting at O and ∠CAB = 30°. (ii) Rectangle PQRS with diagonals meeting at O and ∠QOR = 110°.
steps_tex: (i): $OA = OB$, because the diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so $\angle ABD = \angle CAB = 30^\circ$.
$\angle CAD = 90 - 30 = 60$, and $OA = OD$ gives $\angle ADB = 60$.
In the same way $\angle BDC = 30$, $\angle ACD = 30$ and $\angle ACB = 60$.
At $O$: $\angle AOB = 180 - 60 = 120$ and $\angle AOD = 180 - 120 = 60$.
(ii) $\angle POS = \angle QOR = 110$ (vertically opposite), and $\angle QOP = \angle ROS = 180 - 110 = 70$.
In isosceles $\triangle QOR$ the base angles add to $180 - 110 = 70$, so $\angle OQR = \angle ORQ = 35$.
$\angle OQP = 90 - 35 = 55$, and in the same way $\angle OPQ = \angle ORS = \angle OSR = 55$ and $\angle OPS = \angle OSP = 35$.
item.answer_tex: (i) $\angle ABD = 30^\circ$, $\angle CAD = 60^\circ$, $\angle ADB = 60^\circ$, $\angle BDC = 30^\circ$, $\angle ACD = 30^\circ$, $\angle ACB = 60^\circ$, with $120^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ at $O$; (ii) $\angle POS = 110^\circ$, $\angle QOP = \angle ROS = 70^\circ$, $\angle OQR = \angle ORQ = 35^\circ$, $\angle OQP = \angle OPQ = \angle ORS = \angle OSR = 55^\circ$, $\angle OPS = \angle OSP = 35^\circ$
steps: (i) OA = OB, because the diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so ∠ABD = ∠CAB = 30°.
∠CAD = 90 − 30 = 60, and OA = OD gives ∠ADB = 60.
In the same way ∠BDC = 30, ∠ACD = 30 and ∠ACB = 60.
(ii) ∠POS = ∠QOR = 110 (vertically opposite), and ∠QOP = ∠ROS = 180 − 110 = 70.
In isosceles ∆QOR the base angles add to 180 − 110 = 70, so ∠OQR = ∠ORQ = 35.
∠OQP = 90 − 35 = 55, and in the same way ∠OPQ = ∠ORS = ∠OSR = 55 and ∠OPS = ∠OSP = 35.
item.text:
$1$. (i): $OA = OB$, because the diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so $\angle ABD = \angle CAB = 30^\circ$.
$2$. $\angle CAD = 90 - 30 = 60$, and $OA = OD$ gives $\angle ADB = 60$.
$3$. In the same way $\angle BDC = 30$, $\angle ACD = 30$ and $\angle ACB = 60$.
$4$. At $O$: $\angle AOB = 180 - 60 = 120$ and $\angle AOD = 180 - 120 = 60$.
$5$. (ii) $\angle POS = \angle QOR = 110$ (vertically opposite), and $\angle QOP = \angle ROS = 180 - 110 = 70$.

Answer: (i) $\angle ABD = 30^\circ$, $\angle CAD = 60^\circ$, $\angle ADB = 60^\circ$, $\angle BDC = 30^\circ$, $\angle ACD = 30^\circ$, $\angle ACB = 60^\circ$, with $120^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ at $O$; (ii) $\angle POS = 110^\circ$, $\angle QOP = \angle ROS = 70^\circ$, $\angle OQR = \angle ORQ = 35^\circ$, $\angle OQP = \angle OPQ = \angle ORS = \angle OSR = 55^\circ$, $\angle OPS = \angle OSP = 35^\circ$

item.question: Four quadrilaterals each have all angles 90°: 5 cm by 2 cm, 6 cm by 3.6 cm, 5 cm by 1 cm, and 4 cm by 4 cm. Which are rectangles and which are squares?
steps_tex: A rectangle is a quadrilateral whose angles are all $90^\circ$, so all four are rectangles.
A square also needs all four sides equal.
Only the $4\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ figure has equal sides.
item.answer_tex: All four are rectangles; only the $4\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ one is also a square

item.question: Construct a square with a diagonal of 8 cm.
steps_tex: Draw $AC = 8\text{ cm}$ and mark its midpoint $O$, so $OA = OC = 4\text{ cm}$.
Draw the line through $O$ perpendicular to $AC$.
On it mark $B$ and $D$ on opposite sides of $O$ with $OB = OD = 4\text{ cm}$.
Join $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ in order.
The diagonals are equal, bisect each other and meet at $90^\circ$, so $ABCD$ is a square.
item.answer_tex: $ABCD$, with diagonals $AC = BD = 8\text{ cm}$ crossing at right angles at their midpoints, is the square

The diagonals are equal, bisect each other and meet at 90°, so ABCD is a square.

item.question: In square ABCD the diagonal AC is drawn. Find ∠DAC and ∠DCA.
steps_tex: In $\triangle ADC$ the angle at $D$ is a right angle, so $\angle DAC$ and $\angle DCA$ share $180 - 90 = 90$.
$AD = DC$, so the angles opposite them are equal: $\angle DAC = \angle DCA$.
So each is $90 \div 2 = 45$.
item.answer_tex: $\angle DAC = \angle DCA = 45^\circ$, so the diagonal bisects the right angles
steps: In ∆ADC the angle at D is a right angle, so ∠DAC and ∠DCA share 180 − 90 = 90.

item.answer: ∠DAC = ∠DCA = 45°, so the diagonal bisects the right angles

item.question: Consider a circle with centre O. Line segments PL and AM are two perpendicular diameters of the circle. What is the figure APML? Reason and/or experiment to figure this out.
steps_tex: $AM$ and $PL$ are the diagonals of $APML$.
Both are diameters, so they are equal.
Both pass through the centre $O$ and $OA = OM = OP = OL$ (radii), so they bisect each other.
They are perpendicular, so they meet at $90^\circ$.
Equal diagonals that bisect each other at $90^\circ$ make a square.

They are perpendicular, so they meet at 90°.
Equal diagonals that bisect each other at 90° make a square.
item.text:

$2$. Both are diameters, so they are equal.
$3$. Both pass through the centre $O$ and $OA = OM = OP = OL$ (radii), so they bisect each other.
$4$. They are perpendicular, so they meet at $90^\circ$.
$5$. Equal diagonals that bisect each other at $90^\circ$ make a square.
Answer: $APML$ is a square

item.question: Construct a square with diagonal 6 cm without using a protractor.
steps_tex: Draw $AB = 6\text{ cm}$.
With the compass open more than $3\text{ cm}$, draw arcs from $A$ and from $B$ on both sides of $AB$; join the two crossing points. This line is perpendicular to $AB$ through its midpoint $O$.
With the compass set to $3\text{ cm}$ and centre $O$, mark $C$ and $D$ on this line on opposite sides of $AB$.
Join $A$, $C$, $B$ and $D$ in order.
The diagonals are $6\text{ cm}$ each, bisect each other and meet at $90^\circ$, so $ACBD$ is a square.
item.answer_tex: $ACBD$ is the square, with diagonals $AB = CD = 6\text{ cm}$
steps: Draw AB = 6 cm.

item.question: CASE is a square. The points U, V, W and X are the midpoints of the sides of the square. What type of quadrilateral is UVWX? Find this by using geometric reasoning, as well as by construction and measurement. Find other ways of constructing a square within a square such that the vertices of the inner square lie on the sides of the outer square.
steps_tex: At each corner of $CASE$ the two half sides are equal and the corner angle is $90^\circ$.
So the four corner triangles are congruent by $SAS$, and $UV = VW = WX = XU$.
Each corner triangle is isosceles and right-angled, so its base angles are $45^\circ$ each.
On a side, the two $45^\circ$ angles and the angle of $UVWX$ make a straight angle: $180 - 45 - 45 = 90$.
$UVWX$ has four equal sides and four right angles, so it is a square.
Marking four points the same distance from each corner, all going the same way round, again gives four congruent right triangles and so another square.
item.answer_tex: $UVWX$ is a square; any four points at the same distance from the corners, taken the same way round, also make a square
